glance_takeaway: This is an engineering post-mortem of INC-1194, a June 24 partial outage of ledgerline's invoicing API lasting 4h17m with peak 31.2% of requests erroring, 2,312 customer orgs affected and ~$41,300 in SLA credits. The main message is that there was no single root cause: a 14:02 deploy introducing a leading-wildcard LIKE search (full scan of 274.2M rows) acted as trigger, amplified by pre-existing vacuum debt (38.1M dead tuples below the autovacuum threshold) and a no-jitter retry storm that saturated the shared pgbouncer pool (80/80), producing a platform-wide partial outage; removing any one leg would have made June 24 a minor degradation. It was resolved by a feature flag off at 17:05 (rollback impossible), closed 18:19, with zero data loss.

render_issues: none in the capture — all five Mermaid diagrams rendered correctly in full.png. Note the page depends on CDN-loaded mermaid@11 at view time; offline or no-JS viewing would show raw diagram source.
strengths: Near-complete factual coverage: 15/16 facts land, with exact figures (57% killed, 4.7x/15,020 rpm, cl_waiting 1,437, 38.1M dead tuples vs 54.9M threshold) preserved in diagram nodes.

The causal structure the brief demands is the literal shape of the first diagram — trigger + two amplifiers converging on the pool — with a counterfactual caption ('remove any one leg...') that nails T1 above the fold.
Every DB mechanism gets the one-line gloss the audience needs (dead tuples, covering index, pgbouncer pooling, B-tree anchoring), placed in captions right under the diagram that uses it.

Diagram type matches content: flowchart for causality, phased TD chain for the timeline, sequence diagram for the retry feedback loop, mapping for fixes-to-legs; blameless tone explicitly preserved ('Four systemic gaps — not responder error').
weaknesses: T2 (68-minute detection lag) and T4 (layered scheduled fixes) are invisible at a glance — they live below the fold, so the 10-second read only delivers T1 and half of T3.

Endpoint-group latency impact (F3: p50 85ms→2.9s, p99 420ms→28.4s), the 19.1% average error rate, and 362k failed requests are missing — the 'how bad was it' quantification leans entirely on the peak number.

Mermaid default rendering costs legibility: small node text, awkward long edge sweeps in the overview, a space-wasting single-column timeline, and node fill colors whose semantics shift between diagrams with no legend.
The remediation flowchart is a table dressed as a diagram (five parallel arrows all labeled 'targets'), and owner names were dropped for team names.
evaluator_notes: Accuracy is formulaic: 15 conveyed, 1 absent (F3), 0 distorted, 0 contradicted → 10*15/16 = 9.4. Several 'conveyed' marks are partial (F1 no SEV-1, F2 peak only, F4 no percentages/contract count, F16 teams not owners); none rise to distortion. Glance score reflects that the recorded glance takeaway captured T1 fully and T3 partially but nothing of T2/T4. Depth is strong for the brief's EM audience thanks to the glosses, but the page is at the upper edge of node-text density; sequence-diagram notation may slow a non-expert. structure_nav has clear sections but no TOC/anchors. visual_craft is honest and purposeful but generic-Mermaid in polish.
